title: Myth vs Fact: Does Steeper Pipe Slope Prevent Clogs?
description: A common misconception in drainage piping is that installing horizontal branch lines at a steep angle will clear waste faster and prevent clogs. In reality, drainage systems rely on a specific liquid-to-solid ratio to carry waste effectively. When a pipe's slope is too steep, water flows rapidly past solids, leaving dry debris stranded inside the pipe. Over time, these accumulated solids cause severe blockages. Always adhere to code-specified pitch requirements—typically 1/4 inch per foot for standard branch lines—to maintain adequate scouring velocity without separating liquids from solids.

Myth vs Fact: Does Steeper Pipe Slope Prevent Clogs?

A common misconception in drainage piping is that installing horizontal branch lines at a steep angle will clear waste faster and prevent clogs. In reality, drainage systems rely on a specific liquid-to-solid ratio to carry waste effectively. When a pipe's slope is too steep, water flows rapidly past solids, leaving dry debris stranded inside the pipe. Over time, these accumulated solids cause severe blockages. Always adhere to code-specified pitch requirements—typically 1/4 inch per foot for standard branch lines—to maintain adequate scouring velocity without separating liquids from solids.
